records.source: שׁוֹטְט֞וּ בְּחוּצ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם וּרְאוּ־נָ֤א וּדְעוּ֙ וּבַקְשׁ֣וּ בִרְחוֹבוֹתֶ֔יהָ אִם־תִּמְצְא֣וּ אִ֔ישׁ אִם־יֵ֛שׁ עֹשֶׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אֱמוּנָ֑ה וְאֶסְלַ֖ח לָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Roam through [the] streets of Jerusalem, and see, please, and know, and seek in her squares, if you find a person, if there is [one] doing justice, seeking faithfulness, and I will forgive her.
pieces: Roam the streets of Jerusalem; look around and take note; search her public squares. \q See if you can find a single person, \q one who acts justly and seeks to be faithful, \q and I will pardon the city.

L.1: Run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, and look, please, and take note, and search in her squares, \q if you can find a person, \q if there is one who does justice, who seeks faithfulness, \q and I will pardon her.

R.1: Go up and down the streets of Jerusalem. Look around and pay attention. Search the city squares. \q See if you can find even one person \q who does what is right and tries to be faithful and true. \q If you can, I will forgive the city.

decisions.choice: search for one person, and I will forgive: an echo of Abraham pleading for Sodom
decisions.reason: Abraham asked God whether he would spare Sodom for fifty righteous people, and bargained down to ten (Genesis 18:22-32). Here God asks for less than Abraham dared to: if even one person in Jerusalem does justice, he will pardon the whole city. The search fails (verses 4-5), which shows how deep the city's guilt is (compare Ezekiel 22:30).

decisions.choice: faithfulness: being true to one's word and dependable in dealings with others
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the root meaning firm or reliable. Set beside "doing justice", it means honesty and keeping faith with people and with God; verse 2 shows its opposite, swearing to a lie, and verse 3 says God's eyes look for it.

decisions.choice: God is the speaker; the people told to search are not named
decisions.reason: The commands are plural and no one is named. "I will forgive her" shows that God himself is speaking. The searchers may be the prophet and anyone who will look; the point is the result of the search, not who makes it. "Her" is Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the city
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the city" for the pronoun "her", so the reader knows that the one to be pardoned is Jerusalem.

records.heading: Search for one who acts justly

records.source: וְאִ֥ם חַי־יְהֹוָ֖ה יֹאמֵ֑רוּ לָכֵ֥ן לַשֶּׁ֖קֶר יִשָּׁבֵֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: And though "[As] lives Yahweh" they say, surely to falsehood they swear.
pieces: Even when they say, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," \q they are swearing to a lie.

L.2: And though they say, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," \q surely they swear falsely.

R.2: They make promises with the words "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives." \q But even then their promises are lies.

decisions.choice: "as the LORD lives": an oath that calls God as witness
decisions.reason: Israelites swore by the life of God to show that they were telling the truth (Judges 8:19; 1 Samuel 14:39; Ruth 3:13). To use God's name this way while lying is the misuse of his name forbidden in Exodus 20:7 and Leviticus 19:12. Jeremiah later says that a true oath by the living God would bring blessing to the nations (4:2).

decisions.choice: surely: the word makes the statement emphatic
decisions.reason: The word usually means "therefore", but "therefore" does not fit here, since swearing falsely is not a result of saying the oath. With a few other verbs it simply makes the statement strong: "even so", "surely".

decisions.choice: make promises with the words ... their promises are lies
decisions.reason: Readable explains what an oath is (a solemn promise) and keeps the oath's words in quotation marks.

decisions.choice: [As] the LORD lives (Literal); As surely as the LORD lives (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The oath is worded as in 4:2.

records.source: יְהֹוָ֗ה עֵינֶיךָ֮ הֲל֣וֹא לֶאֱמוּנָה֒ הִכִּ֤יתָה אֹתָם֙ וְֽלֹא־חָ֔לוּ כִּלִּיתָ֕ם מֵאֲנ֖וּ קַ֣חַת מוּסָ֑ר חִזְּק֤וּ פְנֵיהֶם֙ מִסֶּ֔לַע מֵאֲנ֖וּ לָשֽׁוּב׃
records.gloss: Yahweh, your eyes, [are they] not on faithfulness? You struck them, and not they writhed; you finished them, they refused to take discipline; they made hard their faces more than rock, they refused to return.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do not {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes look for faithfulness? \q You struck them, but they felt no pain; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} crushed them, but they would not accept correction. \q They set their faces harder than rock; \q they would not turn back.

L.3: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, are not {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes on faithfulness? \q You struck them, but they did not writhe; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} finished them off, but they refused to accept correction. \q They made their faces harder than rock; \q they refused to turn back.

R.3: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are looking for people who are faithful. \q You struck these people, but it did not hurt them. \q You nearly wiped them out, but they would not learn their lesson. \q They became harder than a rock. \q They refused to turn back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: the prophet now speaks to God
decisions.reason: The verse addresses God directly ("your eyes", "you struck them"). It is Jeremiah's answer to the search of verse 1: God looks for faithfulness, and the people have none.

decisions.choice: they did not writhe ... you finished them: severe punishment that made no difference
decisions.reason: The first verb is used of trembling or writhing in pain. "Finished them" is strong language for blows that should have been crushing; in context it is not literal destruction, since the people are still there refusing correction. The past disasters were meant to teach them (2:30; Amos 4:6-11).

decisions.choice: made their faces harder than rock: defiant, stubborn refusal
decisions.reason: A hard face is a set, defiant look that refuses to be ashamed or to give way (Ezekiel 3:7-9; Proverbs 21:29).

decisions.choice: turn back: return to God, repent
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Jeremiah uses again and again for Israel turning away from God and for the call to come back to him (3:12, 14, 22; 4:1).

decisions.choice: you are looking for people who are faithful ... nearly wiped them out ... harder than a rock
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a statement, says "nearly wiped them out" so the strong verb is not read as complete destruction, says "harder than a rock" for the hard faces, and names God as the one they refuse to turn back to.

records.source: וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי אַךְ־דַּלִּ֖ים הֵ֑ם נוֹאֲל֕וּ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָדְעוּ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יְהוָ֔ה מִשְׁפַּ֖ט אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I, I said, "Only poor [are] they; they act foolishly, for not they know [the] way of Yahweh, [the] ordinance of their God.
pieces: I said, "These are only the poor; \q they act foolishly because they do not know the way of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q what their God requires.

L.4: And I said, "These are only the poor; \q they act foolishly, for they do not know the way of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the ordinance of their God.

R.4: I said to myself, "These are just poor people. \q They act foolishly because they do not know the way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} wants them to live. \q They do not know what their God requires.

decisions.choice: I said: the prophet says to himself what he thinks; his words run into verse 5
decisions.reason: "I said" often means "I thought" (Genesis 20:11; Isaiah 49:4). Jeremiah reasons that the ones he has seen so far are poor and uneducated, and in verse 5 he plans to go to the great. His words end before the last line of verse 5.

decisions.choice: the poor: the lowly, people without wealth or influence
decisions.reason: The word means weak or poor. Here it is set against "the great" in verse 5: people with little standing and perhaps little teaching, from whom less might be expected.

decisions.choice: ordinance: what God has ordered his people to do
decisions.reason: This is the word for justice in verse 1, used here for God's ruling or requirement, the way he has laid down for them. Jeremiah 8:7 uses it the same way: the birds know their seasons, but God's people do not know the ordinance of the LORD.

decisions.choice: said to myself ... the way the LORD wants them to live
decisions.reason: Readable says "said to myself" because Jeremiah is thinking, and explains "the way of the LORD" as the way of life he asks for.

records.source: אֵֽלֲכָה־לִּ֤י אֶל־הַגְּדֹלִים֙ וַאֲדַבְּרָ֣ה אוֹתָ֔ם כִּ֣י הֵ֗מָּה יָדְעוּ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יְהוָ֔ה מִשְׁפַּ֖ט אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם אַ֣ךְ הֵ֤מָּה יַחְדָּו֙ שָׁ֣בְרוּ עֹ֔ל נִתְּק֖וּ מוֹסֵרֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: I will go, for myself, to the great [ones] and I will speak with them, for they know [the] way of Yahweh, [the] ordinance of their God. But they together have broken [the] yoke, they have torn off [the] bonds.
pieces: I will go to the great and speak with them; \q surely they know the way of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q what their God requires." \q But they too, one and all, had broken the yoke \q and snapped the straps.

L.5: I will go to the great and speak with them, \q for they know the way of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the ordinance of their God." \q But they, all alike, had broken the yoke; \q they had torn off the bonds.

R.5: I will go to the important leaders and talk to them. \q They surely know the way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} wants them to live. \q They know what their God requires." \q But all of them had refused to obey. They were like oxen that had broken their yokes \q and torn off their harness.

decisions.choice: the great: people of rank and power, the leaders
decisions.reason: Set against "the poor" of verse 4, these are the city's leading men, who had wealth, power and the chance to be taught. They should have known God's ways; they turn out to be no better.

decisions.choice: broken the yoke, torn off the bonds: refused to serve God
decisions.reason: A yoke was the wooden bar laid on the necks of working oxen, held on by straps. Israel breaking its yoke is a picture of throwing off God's rule and the covenant they owed him (2:20; Psalm 2:3).

decisions.choice: the last line is what the prophet found, not part of his thought
decisions.reason: "But they" begins Jeremiah's report of what he found when he went to the great: they were all the same as the poor. The word "together" means all of them, rich and poor alike.

decisions.choice: had refused to obey. They were like oxen
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means and then explains it as oxen breaking their yokes.

records.source: עַל־כֵּן֩ הִכָּ֨ם אַרְיֵ֜ה מִיַּ֗עַר זְאֵ֤ב עֲרָבוֹת֙ יְשָׁדְדֵ֔ם נָמֵ֤ר שֹׁקֵד֙ עַל־עָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם כָּל־הַיּוֹצֵ֥א מֵהֵ֖נָּה יִטָּרֵ֑ף כִּ֤י רַבּוּ֙ פִּשְׁעֵיהֶ֔ם עָצְמ֖וּ מְשׁוּבוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Therefore strikes them a lion from [the] forest, a wolf of [the] desert plains devastates them, a leopard watches over their cities; every one going out from them will be torn; for many are their transgressions, numerous their apostasies.
pieces: So a lion from the forest will attack them, a wolf from the desert will ravage them, \q a leopard lies in wait near their towns; \q anyone who goes out will be torn to pieces. \q For their rebellions are many, \q and they have turned away countless times.

L.6: Therefore a lion from the forest will strike them; a wolf of the desert plains will destroy them; \q a leopard is watching against their cities: \q everyone who goes out of them will be torn to pieces, \q for their transgressions are many, \q their turnings away are numerous.

R.6: So a lion will come out of the forest and kill them. A wolf from the desert will tear them apart. \q A leopard will wait outside their towns \q and tear to pieces anyone who comes out. \q This will happen because they have rebelled so often \q and have turned away from God again and again.

decisions.choice: lion, wolf, leopard: wild beasts as a picture of the coming invaders
decisions.reason: Jeremiah has already called the destroyer of nations a lion that has come out of its thicket (4:7). The three animals together picture an enemy that attacks from every side and watches the towns so that no one can leave safely (Hosea 13:7-8; Habakkuk 1:8).

decisions.choice: of the desert plains: the wolf's home in the dry country
decisions.reason: The word means the dry steppe or desert. The same consonants with different vowels mean "evenings", and Habakkuk 1:8 and Zephaniah 3:3 speak of "evening wolves" that hunt at dusk. The vowels of the received text, set beside "from the forest", point to a place.

decisions.choice: the attacks are certain future events
decisions.reason: The first verb is in the form used for completed actions, but the next verbs look forward ("will devastate", "will be torn"). The prophet speaks of the coming disaster as if it had already begun.

decisions.choice: transgressions ... turnings away: rebellion against God and repeated desertion of him
decisions.reason: The first word is used for a subject breaking with his lord. The second, from the verb "turn", is Jeremiah's word for Israel's turning away from God (2:19; 3:22, where God promises to heal it).

decisions.choice: turned away from God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one they have turned from, which the Hebrew word implies.

records.source: אֵ֤י לָזֹאת֙ אֶֽסְלַֽח־לָ֔ךְבָּנַ֣יִךְ עֲזָב֔וּנִי וַיִּשָּׁבְע֖וּ בְּלֹ֣א אֱלֹהִ֑ים וָאַשְׂבִּ֤עַ אוֹתָם֙ וַיִּנְאָ֔פוּ וּבֵ֥ית זוֹנָ֖ה יִתְגֹּדָֽדוּ׃
records.gloss: How for this will I forgive you? Your children have forsaken me and sworn by no gods. And I fed them full, and they committed adultery, and [at the] house of a prostitute they trooped.
pieces: How can I forgive you for this? \q Your children have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} \q and sworn by what are no gods at all. \q I filled them with food, yet they committed adultery \q and crowded into the house of a prostitute.

L.7: How can I pardon you for this? \q Your children have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} \q and sworn by those who are not gods. \q I fed them to the full, yet they committed adultery \q and thronged to the house of a prostitute.

R.7: How can I forgive you for this, Jerusalem? \q Your people have left {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q They make promises in the names of gods that are not real. \q I gave them plenty to eat, but they committed adultery. \q They crowded into the houses of prostitutes.

decisions.choice: you, your children: Jerusalem, pictured as a mother, and her people
decisions.reason: "You" is feminine and singular: God speaks to the city as in verse 1 ("her"). Her children are the people who live in her.

decisions.choice: sworn by no gods: taken oaths in the names of gods that are not gods at all
decisions.reason: Verse 2 said they swear falsely by the LORD; here they swear by other gods. "No gods" says what those gods are: nothing (2:11; Deuteronomy 32:21).

decisions.choice: I fed them to the full
alternatives: I made them take an oath
decisions.reason: The vowels of the received text read "I satisfied them", which sets God's generous care against their unfaithfulness (Deuteronomy 32:15; Hosea 13:6). The same consonants, read with a different letter, would mean "I made them swear", that is, bound them by covenant oath, which would echo the oaths earlier in the verse.

decisions.choice: trooped: went in crowds
alternatives: they gashed themselves at a prostitute's house
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "cut oneself", as mourners and worshipers of other gods did (16:6; 1 Kings 18:28), and some take it so here. It is related to the word for a band or troop, and the phrase "to the house of a prostitute" suits going there in crowds.

decisions.choice: adultery and prostitution: real sexual sin, and also a picture of serving other gods
decisions.reason: Verse 8 speaks of men lusting after their neighbors' wives, so actual adultery is meant. Jeremiah also uses adultery and prostitution for Israel's worship of other gods (3:1-9), and the two belong together in this verse.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem ... your people
decisions.reason: Readable names the city spoken to and says "your people" for her children.

records.source: סוּסִ֥ים מְיֻזָּנִ֖ים מַשְׁכִּ֣ים הָי֑וּ אִ֛ישׁ אֶל־אֵ֥שֶׁת רֵעֵ֖הוּ יִצְהָֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: Horses well-fed, lusty, they were; each to [the] wife of his neighbor they neigh.
pieces: They are like well-fed, lusty stallions; \q each one neighs for his neighbor's wife.

L.8: They were well-fed, lusty horses; \q each neighs after his neighbor's wife.

R.8: They are like strong, well-fed horses that are eager to mate. \q Each man calls out with desire for another man's wife.

decisions.choice: well-fed, lusty: words for horses strong and eager to mate
decisions.reason: Both words are rare and their exact sense is uncertain. The first is usually taken to mean well fed (compare "I fed them to the full", verse 7); the second may mean in heat, or roaming about. Either way the picture is of strong animals driven by desire.

decisions.choice: neighing: open, shameless lust
decisions.reason: A stallion neighing for a mare is a picture of desire that does not hide itself. Jeremiah uses the same word for Jerusalem's "neighings" among her adulteries (13:27).

decisions.choice: his neighbor's wife: the commandments against adultery and coveting
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls Exodus 20:14, 17 and Leviticus 20:10. The men of the city break the commandments with no shame.

decisions.choice: like ... stallions / like strong, well-fed horses
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "like" so the picture is read as a comparison.

records.source: הַֽעַל־אֵ֥לֶּה לוֹא־אֶפְקֹ֖ד נְאֻם־יְהֹוָ֑ה וְאִם֙ בְּג֣וֹי אֲשֶׁר־כָּזֶ֔ה לֹ֥א תִתְנַקֵּ֖ם נַפְשִֽׁי׃ס
records.gloss: For these not will I punish? declares Yahweh; and on a nation which [is] like this not will avenge itself my soul?
pieces: Should I not punish them for these things? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q On a nation such as this \q should I not take vengeance?

L.9: Shall I not punish for these things? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q And on a nation such as this \q shall not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul avenge itself?

R.9: Should I not punish them for doing these things? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Should I not pay back a nation like this?

decisions.choice: questions that expect the answer yes
decisions.reason: God asks the people to judge for themselves: after all he has described, can he fail to punish? The same two questions close the next part of the chapter (verse 29) and come again in 9:8.

decisions.choice: my soul avenge itself: I myself take vengeance
decisions.reason: "Soul" here stands for the person: God himself. Vengeance in God's mouth is not spite but the just act of a king and covenant Lord putting right a wrong done against him (Deuteronomy 32:35, 41; Isaiah 1:24).

decisions.choice: take vengeance / pay back
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "take vengeance" and "pay back" for the Hebrew "my soul avenge itself", which is not natural English.

records.source: עֲל֤וּ בְשָׁרוֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ וְשַׁחֵ֔תוּ וְכָלָ֖ה אַֽל־תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ הָסִ֨ירוּ֙ נְטִ֣ישׁוֹתֶ֔יהָ כִּ֛י ל֥וֹא לַיהוָ֖ה הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: Go up through her vine-rows and destroy, but a full end do not make; remove her branches, for not to Yahweh [are] they.
pieces: Go up through her vineyard rows and ruin them, \q but do not destroy her completely. \q Cut away her branches; \q they do not belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.10: Go up through her vine-rows and destroy, \q but do not make a full end; \q strip away her branches, \q for they do not belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.10: You invaders, go through the vineyards of Jerusalem and destroy them. \q But do not destroy everything. \q Cut off the branches, \q because they do not belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: vine-rows, branches: God's people pictured as a vineyard
decisions.reason: God had planted Israel as a choice vine (2:21; Isaiah 5:1-7; Psalm 80:9-12). The branches stripped away are the people who have become wild and no longer belong to the one who planted them.

decisions.choice: the people commanded are not named; they are the enemies God sends
decisions.reason: The plural commands go to those who will destroy the vineyard. In the setting of verses 6 and 15-17 they are the invading nation, here acting at God's command.

decisions.choice: do not make a full end: judgment that leaves a remnant
decisions.reason: The words are close to 4:27 and come again in verse 18. However severe the punishment, God does not wipe out his people entirely.

decisions.choice: You invaders ... the vineyards of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names those addressed and the city whose vineyards they are. Both come from the context, not from words in the verse.

records.source: כִּי֩ בָג֨וֹד בָּגְד֜וּ בִּ֗י בֵּ֧ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וּבֵ֥ית יְהוּדָ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: For dealing treacherously they have dealt treacherously with me, [the] house of Israel and [the] house of Judah, declares Yahweh.
pieces: For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken faith with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} completely, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.11: For they have utterly betrayed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the house of Israel and the house of Judah, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.11: The people of Israel and the people of Judah have been completely unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: betrayed: broken faith, as an unfaithful wife does
decisions.reason: The verb is used of breaking a trust, often of a wife unfaithful to her husband (3:20; Malachi 2:14). Doubling the verb makes it strong: they have betrayed God completely.

decisions.choice: the house of Israel and the house of Judah: the northern and southern kingdoms
decisions.reason: The northern kingdom, Israel, had already been taken into exile by Assyria in 722 BC; Judah remained. Jeremiah names both as one unfaithful people (3:6-11).

decisions.choice: the people of Israel and the people of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of" for "the house of".

records.source: כִּֽחֲשׁוּ֙ בַּיהוָ֔ה וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹא־ה֑וּא וְלֹא־תָב֤וֹא עָלֵ֨ינוּ֙ רָעָ֔ה וְחֶ֥רֶב וְרָעָ֖ב ל֥וֹא נִרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: They have lied about Yahweh and said, "Not he; and not will come upon us evil, and sword and famine not we will see.
pieces: They have told lies about {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q they have said, "He will do nothing! \q No harm will come to us; \q we will not see sword or famine.

L.12: They have spoken falsely about {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q and said, "Not {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}! \q Disaster will not come upon us, \q and sword and famine we will not see.

R.12: They have told lies about {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q They said, "He will not do anything. \q Nothing bad will happen to us. \q We will not have to face war or famine.

decisions.choice: spoken falsely about: denied the truth about God
decisions.reason: The verb means to deny or to deal falsely. They deny what God has said through his prophets, that he will act against their sin (Isaiah 59:13; Job 31:28).

decisions.choice: "Not he": he will not act
decisions.reason: The two words can mean "he does not exist" or "he will do nothing". Here they are not a denial that God exists but a refusal to believe he will act or judge (Psalm 10:4, 11; Zephaniah 1:12).

decisions.choice: sword and famine: the disasters the covenant warned of
decisions.reason: War and hunger are among the curses Moses said would come on a disobedient people (Leviticus 26:25-26; Deuteronomy 32:24-25). The false prophets of 14:13-15 promise the same thing as these people say here.

decisions.choice: He will do nothing / He will not do anything
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "Not he" means (meaning decision m2).

records.source: וְהַנְּבִיאִים֙ יִֽהְי֣וּ לְר֔וּחַ וְהַדִּבֵּ֖ר אֵ֣ין בָּהֶ֑ם כֹּ֥ה יֵעָשֶׂ֖ה לָהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And the prophets will become wind, and the word not [is] in them; thus will be done to them."
pieces: The prophets are nothing but wind; \q the word is not in them. \q Let what they threaten happen to them!"

L.13: And the prophets will become wind, \q and the word is not in them; \q thus let it be done to them!"

R.13: The prophets are just full of air. \q God does not speak through them. \q Let the things they warn about happen to them instead!"

decisions.choice: the people are still speaking, mocking the prophets who warn them
alternatives: God's verdict on the false prophets
decisions.reason: The verse is read here as the end of the people's words from verse 12: the prophets who announce sword and famine are empty, and their threats should fall on themselves. Verse 14 then answers "because you have spoken this word". It can also be read as God's own sentence on the false prophets, though it is God's true prophets whom the people mock in this setting.

decisions.choice: wind ... the word: wordplay on wind and spirit
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for wind also means spirit. The mockers say the prophets have no spirit from God, only wind, and that "the word", God's word, is not in them. The noun for "word" here is rare and means the thing spoken.

decisions.choice: thus let it be done to them: a wish or curse
alternatives: thus it will be done to them
decisions.reason: The words wish on the prophets the disaster they have announced for others.

decisions.choice: God does not speak through them ... instead
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the word is not in them" and adds "instead" to show who the threat is turned against.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י צְבָא֔וֹת יַ֚עַן דַּבֶּרְכֶ֔ם אֶת־הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה הִנְנִ֣י נֹתֵן֩ דְּבָרַ֨י בְּפִ֜יךָ לְאֵ֗שׁ וְהָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֛ה עֵצִ֖ים וַאֲכָלָֽתַם׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh, God of hosts: Because you have spoken this word, see, I am making my words in your mouth fire, and this people wood, and it will devour them.
pieces: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Armies, says this: \q Because you people have spoken these words, \q I am making {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words in your mouth a fire, \q and this people the wood, and the fire will burn them up.

L.14: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of hosts: \q Because you have spoken this word, \q see, I am making {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words in your mouth a fire, \q and this people wood, and it will consume them.

R.14: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Armies, says: \q You people have said these things. \q So, Jeremiah, I will make the words I give you to speak like a fire. \q These people will be like wood, and the fire will burn them up.

decisions.choice: you have spoken: the people; your mouth: the prophet
decisions.reason: "You have spoken" is plural and means those who spoke in verses 12-13. "Your mouth" is singular: God turns to Jeremiah, whose mouth he filled with his words when he called him (1:9).

decisions.choice: my words a fire, this people wood: God's word will bring about the judgment it announces
decisions.reason: The people called the prophets wind; God makes the prophet's words fire. What Jeremiah speaks will come true and destroy those who mock it (20:9; 23:29).

decisions.choice: the God of hosts: the God who commands the armies of heaven
decisions.reason: "Hosts" means armies: the angels and the stars, and at times Israel's own forces. The title is explained at Isaiah 1:9.

decisions.choice: God of Armies
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, Balanced and Readable say "Armies" for "hosts", which is no longer an everyday word for an army.

decisions.choice: you people ... Jeremiah
decisions.reason: English "you" does not show the change from plural to singular, so Balanced says "you people" and Readable also names Jeremiah.

records.heading: A nation from far away

records.source: הִנְנִ֣י מֵבִיא֩ עֲלֵיכֶ֨ם גּ֧וֹי מִמֶּרְחָ֛ק בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נְאֻם־יְהֹוָ֑ה גּ֣וֹי׀אֵיתָ֣ן ה֗וּא גּ֤וֹי מֵעוֹלָם֙ ה֔וּא גּ֚וֹי לֹא־תֵדַ֣ע לְשֹׁנ֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁמַ֖ע מַה־יְדַבֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: See, I am bringing upon you a nation from afar, house of Israel, declares Yahweh; a nation enduring it [is], a nation from long ago it [is], a nation whose language not you know, and not you will understand what it says.
pieces: House of Israel, I am bringing a nation from far away against you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q It is a nation that endures, a nation from ancient times, \q a nation whose language you do not know; \q you will not understand what they say.

L.15: See, I am bringing against you a nation from afar, house of Israel, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q It is an enduring nation, it is an ancient nation, \q a nation whose language you do not know, \q and you will not understand what it says.

R.15: People of Israel, I am going to bring a nation from far away to attack you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q It is a strong nation that has lasted a long time. It is a very old nation. \q You do not know its language. \q You will not understand what its people say.

decisions.choice: a nation from afar whose language you do not know: the covenant curse
decisions.reason: Moses warned that if Israel turned from God he would bring against them a nation from far away, whose language they would not understand (Deuteronomy 28:49). Isaiah used the same picture (5:26; 28:11; 33:19).

decisions.choice: enduring: lasting and strong
decisions.reason: The word is used of streams that never run dry (Amos 5:24; Deuteronomy 21:4) and of what is firm and lasting. With "from long ago" it describes a nation with a long history and staying power.

decisions.choice: the nation is not named
decisions.reason: Jeremiah has spoken of disaster coming from the north (1:14; 4:6; 6:22). Later chapters name the enemy as Babylon (20:4; 25:9), but here it is left unnamed and the more fearful for it.

decisions.choice: House of Israel / People of Israel first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the people addressed at the start of the sentence, where English puts a name called out.

records.source: אַשְׁפָּת֖וֹ כְּקֶ֣בֶר פָּת֑וּחַ כֻּלָּ֖ם גִּבּוֹרִֽים׃
records.gloss: Its quiver [is] like a grave open; all of them [are] mighty men.
pieces: Their quiver is like an open grave; \q they are all mighty warriors.

L.16: Its quiver is like an open grave; \q all of them are mighty warriors.

R.16: Their arrows bring death, like a grave that is open and waiting. \q All their soldiers are strong fighters.

decisions.choice: a quiver like an open grave: every arrow brings death
decisions.reason: A quiver held a soldier's arrows. Comparing it to an open grave says that its arrows will fill graves: the enemy's archers kill without fail.

decisions.choice: mighty warriors: strong, experienced fighting men
decisions.reason: The word means a mighty man, and in war a seasoned soldier (Judges 6:12; 2 Samuel 23:8).

decisions.choice: Their arrows bring death
decisions.reason: Readable says what the quiver stands for, since many readers will not know the word.

records.source: וְאָכַ֨ל קְצִֽירְךָ֜ וְלַחְמֶ֗ךָ יֹאכְלוּ֙ בָּנֶ֣יךָ וּבְנוֹתֶ֔יךָ יֹאכַ֤ל צֹאנְךָ֙ וּבְקָרֶ֔ךָ יֹאכַ֥ל גַּפְנְךָ֖ וּתְאֵנָתֶ֑ךָ יְרֹשֵׁ֞שׁ עָרֵ֣י מִבְצָרֶ֗יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֛ה בּוֹטֵ֥חַ בָּהֵ֖נָּה בֶּחָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: And it will eat your harvest and your bread; they will eat your sons and your daughters; it will eat your flock and your herd; it will eat your vine and your fig tree; it will shatter your fortified cities, in which you trust, with the sword.
pieces: They will devour your harvest and your food; they will devour your sons and your daughters; \q they will devour your flocks and your herds; \q they will devour your vines and your fig trees. \q With the sword they will break down your fortified towns, the towns you trust in.

L.17: It will eat up your harvest and your bread; they will eat up your sons and your daughters; \q it will eat up your flocks and your herds; \q it will eat up your vines and your fig trees; \q with the sword it will shatter your fortified cities, in which you trust.

R.17: They will eat up your crops and your food. They will kill your sons and your daughters. \q They will eat up your sheep, goats and cattle. \q They will eat up your grapes and figs. \q Their swords will destroy the strong, walled cities that you trust to keep you safe.

decisions.choice: eat ... eat ... eat ... eat: the invading nation consumes everything
decisions.reason: The verb "eat" comes four times, a hammering repetition. "It" is the nation of verse 15; once the verb is plural, for its soldiers. "You" is singular: Israel as one people.

decisions.choice: eat your sons and daughters: kill them
decisions.reason: The enemy will devour the people as it devours the crops: "eat" stands for destroying, as in 3:24, where shame "ate" the sons and daughters.

decisions.choice: the covenant warning of a nation that eats the land and breaks down its trusted walls
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 28:31-33 and 51-52 warn that a foreign nation would eat the produce of the land and the herds, and besiege the high fortified walls in which Israel trusted. Jeremiah's list follows that warning.

decisions.choice: shatter: beat down
decisions.reason: The verb means to break or beat down, as of ruined buildings (Malachi 1:4).

decisions.choice: kill your sons ... sheep, goats and cattle ... grapes and figs
decisions.reason: Readable says "kill" where the eating is of people, and names the animals and fruit plainly.

records.source: וְגַ֛ם בַּיָּמִ֥ים הָהֵ֖מָּה נְאֻם־יְהֹוָ֑ה לֹֽא־אֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה אִתְּכֶ֖ם כָּלָֽה׃
records.gloss: And even in those days, declares Yahweh, not will I make with you a full end.
pieces: Yet even in those days, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q I will not destroy you completely.

L.18: Yet even in those days, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q I will not make a full end of you.

R.18: But even at that time, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q I will not destroy all of you.

decisions.choice: not a full end: God will keep a remnant
decisions.reason: As in verse 10 and 4:27, God limits the destruction. The verse leads into verse 19, where the survivors in exile ask why it has happened.

decisions.choice: destroy you completely / destroy all of you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "destroy completely" for the Hebrew "make a full end", as in verse 10.

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ כִּ֣י תֹאמְר֔וּ תַּ֣חַת מֶ֗ה עָשָׂ֨ה יְהֹוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛ינוּ לָ֖נוּ אֶת־כָּל־אֵ֑לֶּה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר עֲזַבְתֶּ֤ם אוֹתִי֙ וַתַּעַבְד֞וּ אֱלֹהֵ֤י נֵכָר֙ בְּאַרְצְכֶ֔ם כֵּ֚ן תַּעַבְד֣וּ זָרִ֔ים בְּאֶ֖רֶץ לֹ֥א לָכֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And it will be, when you say, "For what has done Yahweh our God to us all these [things]?" then you will say to them, "Just as you forsook me and served gods of foreignness in your land, so you will serve strangers in a land not yours."
pieces: And when the people ask, "Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God done all this to us?" \q you must answer them, \q "As you abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and served foreign gods in your own land, \q so now you will serve strangers in a land not your own."

L.19: And when you say, "Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God done all these things to us?" \q then you shall say to them, \q "As you have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and served foreign gods in your land, \q so you shall serve strangers in a land that is not yours."

R.19: When the people ask, "Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God done all these things to us?" \q tell them that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says, \q "You left {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and served foreign gods in your own land. \q So now you will serve strangers in a land that does not belong to you."

decisions.choice: when you say ... you shall say: first the people, then the prophet
decisions.reason: "You say" is plural: the people. "You shall say to them" is singular: Jeremiah. The "me" of his answer is God, so the prophet is to give God's own words.

decisions.choice: served foreign gods ... serve strangers: the punishment matches the sin
decisions.reason: Those who chose to serve foreign gods in their own land will serve foreign people in a land not theirs. Moses had warned of the same (Deuteronomy 28:47-48, 64).

decisions.choice: strangers: foreigners, people of another nation
decisions.reason: The word means outsiders, those who do not belong; here the foreign masters of the exiles.

decisions.choice: the people ask ... tell them that the LORD says
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the people" because English "you" cannot show the plural, and Readable adds "that the LORD says" to show whose words the answer gives.

records.source: הַגִּ֥ידוּ זֹ֖את בְּבֵ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְהַשְׁמִיע֥וּהָ בִיהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: Declare this in [the] house of Jacob, and proclaim it in Judah, saying:
pieces: Announce this to the house of Jacob; \q make it heard in Judah:

L.20: Declare this in the house of Jacob, \q and proclaim it in Judah, saying:

R.20: Tell this to the people of Israel. \q Announce it in Judah. Say:

decisions.choice: the house of Jacob: the whole people descended from Jacob
decisions.reason: Jacob is the ancestor named Israel (Genesis 32:29). Beside Judah, "the house of Jacob" means the whole people, as "Israel and Judah" does in verse 11.

decisions.choice: God's speech goes on; the message is his own words
decisions.reason: The plural commands go to unnamed messengers. What they are to proclaim (verses 21-31) is still God speaking in the first person, so it takes no quotation marks.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Israel" for "the house of Jacob", as Isaiah does for the people called Jacob.

records.heading: A stubborn and rebellious people

records.source: שִׁמְעוּ־נָ֣א זֹ֔את עַ֥ם סָכָ֖ל וְאֵ֣ין לֵ֑ב עֵינַ֤יִם לָהֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א יִרְא֔וּ אָזְנַ֥יִם לָהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמָֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: Hear, please, this, people foolish and without heart; eyes [are] to them, and not they see; ears [are] to them, and not they hear.
pieces: Listen to this, you foolish people with no sense, \q you who have eyes and do not see, \q who have ears and do not hear.

L.21: Hear this, you foolish people without heart, \q who have eyes but do not see, \q who have ears but do not hear.

R.21: Listen to this, you foolish people who do not think! \q You have eyes, but you do not see. \q You have ears, but you do not hear.

decisions.choice: without heart: without sense or understanding
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and judgment in Hebrew, so a people without heart has no sense (Hosea 7:11).

decisions.choice: eyes but do not see, ears but do not hear
decisions.reason: Isaiah was sent to a people who would hear and see without understanding (Isaiah 6:9-10), and Moses said that God had not yet given Israel eyes to see or ears to hear (Deuteronomy 29:3). The words also describe idols, which have eyes and ears that do nothing (Psalm 115:5-6): the people have become like the gods they serve. Compare Ezekiel 12:2 and Mark 8:18.

decisions.choice: "you" then "they": the address shifts to a description
decisions.reason: The verse calls to the people directly and then describes them in the third person ("eyes are to them"), as if speaking about them to others.

decisions.choice: You have eyes ... You have ears
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the address in the second person throughout to keep the sentences short and clear.

records.source: הַאוֹתִ֨י לֹא־תִירָ֜אוּ נְאֻם־יְהֹוָ֗ה אִ֤ם מִפָּנַי֙ לֹ֣א תָחִ֔ילוּ אֲשֶׁר־שַׂ֤מְתִּי חוֹל֙ גְּב֣וּל לַיָּ֔ם חָק־עוֹלָ֖ם וְלֹ֣א יַעַבְרֶ֑נְהוּ וַיִּֽתְגָּעֲשׁוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יוּכָ֔לוּ וְהָמ֥וּ גַלָּ֖יו וְלֹ֥א יַעַבְרֻֽנְהוּ׃
records.gloss: Me not will you fear? declares Yahweh; or from before me not will you tremble? who set sand [as a] boundary for the sea, a perpetual decree, and not it will pass it; and they toss, and not they prevail; and they roar, its waves, and not they pass it.
pieces: Do you not fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Will you not tremble in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence? \q I set the sand as the boundary of the sea, \q a lasting decree it cannot cross. \q Its waters may heave, but they cannot win; \q its waves may roar, but they cannot pass beyond it.

L.22: Do you not fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Do you not tremble before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q who placed the sand as a boundary for the sea, \q a perpetual decree, and it cannot pass it? \q Though they toss, they cannot prevail; \q though its waves roar, they cannot pass over it.

R.22: Why are you not afraid of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Why do you not shake with fear in front of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? \q I made the sand a border for the sea. \q It is a rule that will last forever. The sea cannot go past it. \q The waves may toss, but they cannot win. \q They may roar, but they cannot cross that line.

decisions.choice: the sand as the sea's boundary: God the Creator who holds back the sea
decisions.reason: The sea, which seemed wild and endless to Israel, stays within the limit God gave it at creation (Genesis 1:9; Job 38:8-11; Psalm 104:9; Proverbs 8:29). The one who commands the sea deserves to be feared.

decisions.choice: a perpetual decree: a limit fixed by God's command for all time
decisions.reason: The word means something laid down or prescribed, a statute. The sea obeys the rule God set for it; verse 23 says God's people do not.

decisions.choice: questions that expect the answer yes
decisions.reason: The questions mean "Surely you should fear me!"

decisions.choice: Why are you not afraid ... Why do you not shake
decisions.reason: Readable makes the questions "why" questions, which keep their force for young readers.

decisions.choice: Its waters may heave
decisions.reason: Balanced names the waters as the subject of the first verb, which the Hebrew leaves implied; the waves are named in the next line.

records.source: וְלָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ הָיָ֔ה לֵ֖ב סוֹרֵ֣ר וּמוֹרֶ֑ה סָ֖רוּ וַיֵּלֵֽכוּ׃
records.gloss: But to this people there is a heart stubborn and rebellious; they have turned aside and gone.
pieces: But this people has a stubborn, rebellious heart; \q they have turned away and gone off.

L.23: But this people has a stubborn and rebellious heart; \q they have turned aside and gone away.

R.23: But these people are stubborn and they rebel against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q They have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and left.

decisions.choice: stubborn and rebellious: the words for the son who will not obey
decisions.reason: The same pair of words describes the son who will not listen to his parents in Deuteronomy 21:18, 20, and the generation in the wilderness in Psalm 78:8.

decisions.choice: turned aside and gone: unlike the sea, the people do not keep to God's limit
decisions.reason: The sea does not cross the boundary God set for it (verse 22), but God's people have turned aside and walked away from him.

decisions.choice: rebel against me ... turned away from me
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one they rebel against and leave, which the Hebrew implies.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־אָמְר֣וּ בִלְבָבָ֗ם נִ֤ירָא נָא֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הַנֹּתֵ֗ן גֶּ֛שֶׁם יוֹרֶ֥ה וּמַלְק֖וֹשׁ בְּעִתּ֑וֹ שְׁבֻע֛וֹת חֻקּ֥וֹת קָצִ֖יר יִשְׁמָר־לָֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And not they have said in their heart, "Let us fear, please, Yahweh our God, who gives rain, early rain and late rain, in its season, [the] weeks, [the] appointed [times] of harvest he keeps for us."
pieces: They do not say to themselves, "Let us fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, \q who gives the rain in its season, the autumn rain and the spring rain, \q and keeps for us the weeks set for the harvest."

L.24: And they do not say in their heart, "Let us fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, \q who gives rain, the autumn rain and the spring rain, in its season; \q the appointed weeks of harvest {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps for us."

R.24: They do not think, "We should fear and honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. \q He sends the rain at the right time, in the fall and in the spring. \q He makes sure we have the weeks of harvest every year."

decisions.choice: the autumn rain and the spring rain: the two rainy seasons farming depended on
decisions.reason: In Israel the first rains came in October and November, softening the ground for sowing, and the last rains in March and April, filling out the grain before harvest. God promised both to an obedient people (Deuteronomy 11:14).

decisions.choice: the appointed weeks of harvest: the dry weeks of the grain harvest
decisions.reason: The grain harvest ran for seven weeks, from barley to wheat, and ended with the Festival of Weeks (Deuteronomy 16:9-10; Exodus 34:22). God keeps that time dry and settled so that the crop can be gathered.

decisions.choice: fear the LORD: awe and reverence that lead to obedience
decisions.reason: To fear God is to take him seriously as Lord and live in his ways (Deuteronomy 10:12). Verse 22 asked why they do not fear him; here they never think of it, though his gifts come every year.

decisions.choice: fear and honor
decisions.reason: Readable adds "honor" so that "fear" is not read only as terror.

records.source: עֲוֺנוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם הִטּוּ־אֵ֑לֶּה וְחַטֹּ֣אותֵיכֶ֔ם מָנְע֥וּ הַטּ֖וֹב מִכֶּֽם׃
records.gloss: Your iniquities have turned away these, and your sins have withheld the good from you.
pieces: Your guilt has turned these blessings away; \q your sins have kept good things from you.

L.25: Your iniquities have turned these away, \q and your sins have held back the good from you.

R.25: Your sins have stopped these blessings from coming. \q The wrong things you have done have kept good things away from you.

decisions.choice: these: the rains and the harvest of verse 24
decisions.reason: "These" points back to the gifts just named. Jeremiah has already said that the showers were held back because of the people's unfaithfulness (3:3).

decisions.choice: sins have withheld the good: drought as a result of breaking the covenant
decisions.reason: Moses warned that if Israel served other gods, God would shut up the sky and there would be no rain (Deuteronomy 11:16-17; Leviticus 26:19-20).

decisions.choice: iniquities, sins: two words for wrongdoing
decisions.reason: The first stresses guilt and twisted conduct, the second missing the mark. Together they cover all the people's wrong.

decisions.choice: these blessings
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "blessings" so the reader knows what "these" refers to.

records.source: כִּי־נִמְצְא֥וּ בְעַמִּ֖י רְשָׁעִ֑ים יָשׁוּר֙ כְּשַׁ֣ךְ יְקוּשִׁ֔ים הִצִּ֥יבוּ מַשְׁחִ֖ית אֲנָשִׁ֥ים יִלְכֹּֽדוּ׃
records.gloss: For are found among my people wicked [men]; he watches as fowlers crouch; they set a trap; men they catch.
pieces: For there are wicked {{gender:people|men}} among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q They lie in wait like hunters crouching for birds; \q they set a deadly trap and catch human beings.

L.26: For wicked {{gender:people|men}} are found among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people; \q one watches as fowlers crouch; \q they set a trap; they catch {{gender:people|men}}.

R.26: There are wicked {{gender:people|men}} among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q They hide and watch, like hunters waiting to trap birds. \q They set traps to catch people.

decisions.choice: he watches as fowlers crouch: a hard line
alternatives: he watches as one lies in wait for birds
they watch like fowlers in hiding
decisions.reason: The verb is singular ("he watches"), describing each of the wicked, and the word read as "crouch" is rare. The sense is clear enough: they wait in hiding like men catching birds. The exact wording of the line is uncertain.

decisions.choice: trap: literally "destroyer", a deadly snare
decisions.reason: The word means something that destroys. Here it is the trap set for people, one that ruins those caught in it.

decisions.choice: fowlers: bird-catchers, a picture of those who prey on people
decisions.reason: Bird-catchers used nets and snares hidden on the ground (Psalm 124:7; Proverbs 1:17). The wicked set traps for their neighbors in the same way, by fraud and false charges.

decisions.choice: people / men
decisions.reason: The wicked, and those they trap, are not only men, so the inclusive word is the default and "men" is offered through the gender setting.

records.source: כִּכְלוּב֙ מָ֣לֵא ע֔וֹף כֵּ֥ן בָּתֵּיהֶ֖ם מְלֵאִ֣ים מִרְמָ֑ה עַל־כֵּ֥ן גָּדְל֖וּ וַֽיַּעֲשִֽׁירוּ׃
records.gloss: Like a cage full of birds, so their houses [are] full of deceit; therefore they have become great and grown rich.
pieces: Like a basket full of birds, \q their houses are full of what they gained by deceit. \q That is how they have become powerful and rich.

L.27: Like a cage full of birds, \q so their houses are full of deceit; \q therefore they have become great and grown rich.

R.27: A hunter's cage is full of the birds he has caught. \q In the same way, their houses are full of things they got by cheating. \q That is how they became powerful and rich.

decisions.choice: cage: the wicker basket in which a fowler kept the birds he had caught
decisions.reason: The word is used for a basket in Amos 8:1-2. The picture continues the fowlers of verse 26.

decisions.choice: houses full of deceit: full of goods gained by fraud
decisions.reason: As the cage is full of captured birds, their houses are full of what they have taken from others by deceit (Amos 3:10; Micah 6:10-12).

decisions.choice: therefore: this is the way they became rich
decisions.reason: The word gives the cause of their wealth, not a later punishment: their greatness and riches come from their deceit.

decisions.choice: what they gained by deceit / things they got by cheating
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the houses are filled with (meaning decision m2).

records.source: שָׁמְנ֣וּ עָשְׁת֗וּ גַּ֚ם עָֽבְר֣וּ דִבְרֵי־רָ֔ע דִּ֣ין לֹא־דָ֔נוּ דִּ֥ין יָת֖וֹם וְיַצְלִ֑יחוּ וּמִשְׁפַּ֥ט אֶבְיוֹנִ֖ים לֹ֥א שָׁפָֽטוּ׃
records.gloss: They have grown fat, they have become sleek; also they have passed over [in] matters of evil; [the] cause not they have judged, [the] cause of [the] fatherless, and they prosper; and [the] justice of [the] needy not they have judged.
pieces: They have grown fat and sleek; their evil deeds go beyond all limits. \q They do not take up the case, \q the case of the fatherless, yet they prosper; \q they do not defend the rights of the needy.

L.28: They have grown fat, they are sleek; they also overflow with deeds of evil; \q they do not plead the cause, \q the cause of the fatherless, yet they prosper; \q and they do not defend the rights of the needy.

R.28: They are fat and well fed. They keep doing more and more evil things. \q They do not stand up in court for children who have no father, \q and yet they get richer. \q They do not defend the rights of poor people.

decisions.choice: they overflow with deeds of evil: their evil goes past every limit
decisions.reason: The verb means to pass over or beyond. It may mean their evil deeds overflow every bound, or that they pass over, that is overlook, evil deeds when they judge. The first suits the picture of excess in the line before.

decisions.choice: yet they prosper
alternatives: so as to make it succeed
decisions.reason: The verb can be read as the result of their behavior: they ignore the cause of the fatherless and still do well for themselves. Some read it as the purpose of a case properly heard, "so that it might succeed", which would mean the orphan's case.

decisions.choice: the fatherless and the needy: people with no one to defend them
decisions.reason: Children without a father, widows and the poor had no one to speak for them in court. The law and the prophets charge judges and leaders to defend them (Exodus 22:21-23; Deuteronomy 10:18; Isaiah 1:17, 23).

decisions.choice: stand up in court for children who have no father
decisions.reason: Readable explains "plead the cause" as defending someone in court and "the fatherless" as children without a father.

records.source: הַֽעַל־אֵ֥לֶּה לֹֽא־אֶפְקֹ֖ד נְאֻם־יְהֹוָ֑ה אִ֚ם בְּג֣וֹי אֲשֶׁר־כָּזֶ֔ה לֹ֥א תִתְנַקֵּ֖ם נַפְשִֽׁי׃ס
records.gloss: For these not will I punish? declares Yahweh; or on a nation which [is] like this not will avenge itself my soul?
pieces: Should I not punish them for these things? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q On a nation such as this \q should I not take vengeance?

L.29: Shall I not punish for these things? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Or on a nation such as this \q shall not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul avenge itself?

R.29: Should I not punish them for doing these things? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Should I not pay back a nation like this?

decisions.choice: the refrain of verse 9 again
decisions.reason: The questions repeat verse 9 almost word for word, closing the second list of charges as they closed the first. The rendering follows verse 9, and the notes there apply.

decisions.choice: same wording as verse 9
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

records.source: שַׁמָּה֙ וְשַׁ֣עֲרוּרָ֔ה נִהְיְתָ֖ה בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: An appalling and horrible [thing] has happened in the land:
pieces: Something shocking and horrible \q has happened in the land:

L.30: An appalling and horrible thing \q has happened in the land:

R.30: Something terrible and shocking has happened in the land:

decisions.choice: appalling and horrible: a thing that fills people with horror
decisions.reason: The first word means something that makes people stare in horror; the second, a rare word, is used for the shocking things done by Israel and by the prophets of Jerusalem (18:13; 23:14; Hosea 6:10).

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 31
decisions.reason: Verse 31 says what the horrible thing is, so this record ends with a colon.

records.source: הַנְּבִיאִ֞ים נִבְּא֣וּ־בַשֶּׁ֗קֶר וְהַכֹּהֲנִים֙ יִרְדּ֣וּ עַל־יְדֵיהֶ֔ם וְעַמִּ֖י אָ֣הֲבוּ כֵ֑ן וּמַֽה־תַּעֲשׂ֖וּ לְאַחֲרִיתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: The prophets prophesy by falsehood, and the priests rule by their hands, and my people love [it] so; and what will you do at its end?
pieces: The prophets prophesy lies, and the priests rule with the prophets' backing, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people like it this way. \q But what will you do when the end comes?

L.31: The prophets prophesy by falsehood, and the priests rule by their hands, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people love it so. \q But what will you do at its end?

R.31: The prophets tell lies when they speak for God. The priests rule with the support of those prophets. \q And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people like it this way. \q But what will you do when it all comes to an end?

decisions.choice: prophesy by falsehood: speak lies as if they were God's message
decisions.reason: They claim to speak for God but say what he has not said: peace when there is no peace (6:14; 14:14; 23:16-17, 25-26). Jeremiah also speaks of prophets who prophesied by Baal (2:8; 23:13).

decisions.choice: rule by their hands: with the prophets' backing, at their side
alternatives: the priests rule on their own authority
decisions.reason: "By the hands of" means through someone or under someone's direction (1 Chronicles 25:2-3). Here "their" is taken to be the prophets: the priests rule supported and guided by them. It may instead mean that the priests rule by their own hand, on their own authority.

decisions.choice: my people love it so: the people share the guilt
decisions.reason: The leaders are not the only ones to blame. The people want comforting lies and like being ruled this way (Isaiah 30:10; Micah 2:11).

decisions.choice: at its end: when this state of things comes to its outcome
decisions.reason: "Its" is feminine, pointing to the whole situation. When judgment comes, the lies will not protect them.

decisions.choice: with the prophets' backing / with the support of those prophets
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the prophets as the "their" of the Hebrew (meaning decision m2).
